At that time, he had started with fever again and was feeling unwell. Physical examination revealed a mildly impaired general condition without haemodynamic or respiratory instability. No hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy or meningism was observed. He denied dyspnoea, diarrhoea, dysgeusia or anosmia. Vital signs were within the normal range except for fever (38°C).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Ewing’s sarcoma with metastatic pulmonary and bone marrow dissemination
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with fever, asthenia, progressive cough, thoracic urticarial rash, and lower back pain. Initial workup included a Chest X-ray which revealed interstitial infiltrates in both lungs. Blood tests showed elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ferritin, IL-6). A bone marrow biopsy was performed, which showed small, round blue cells, suggestive of solid tumour infiltration, supporting the diagnosis of Ewing's sarcoma with metastatic bone marrow and pulmonary dissemination.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with persistent asthenia, progressive cough, fever, thoracic urticarial rash, and lower back pain.
Chest X-ray showed interstitial infiltrates in both lungs, consistent with pulmonary metastasis.
Blood tests revealed elevated inflammatory markers including C-reactive protein (5.71 mg/dL), ferritin (668 ng/mL), and interleukin 6 (70.9 pg/mL).
Bone marrow biopsy showed small, round blue cells, suggestive of solid tumour infiltration, supporting bone marrow dissemination.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific histopathological confirmation of Ewing's sarcoma (e.g., immunohistochemistry, genetic testing) from the biopsy was not explicitly detailed beyond 'suggestive of solid tumour infiltration'.
The primary tumor location for Ewing's sarcoma was not identified or confirmed in the provided evidence.
Further characterization of pulmonary findings (e.g., Chest CT scan report) was not available.
Imaging findings for lower back pain (e.g., MRI spine, PET-CT report) were not available to identify a primary bone lesion.
